scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants the power of praise across parents, employers, and teachers, then shows why ignoring negative actions fails; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose at about 400 words on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Praise can bring out the best in children, employees, and students alike.
Some people claim that the best way to teach, whether as a parent, employer, or educator, is to praise good actions and ignore bad ones.
I agree that praise is a powerful teaching tool, but I do not believe that ignoring negative actions is ever the best approach.
First, praise encourages people to repeat the behavior we want to see.
When effort is noticed and rewarded, people feel valued and try harder.
For example, an employee whose good work is regularly recognized will usually stay motivated and loyal.
This shows that encouragement can shape behavior more gently and lastingly than constant criticism.
Parents see the same effect when a child praised for kindness becomes eager to be kind again.
Positive attention, in short, teaches people what success looks like.
For this reason, praise deserves a central place in teaching of every kind.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why ignoring bad actions fails

sentences.text: Second, however, ignoring negative actions can be careless and even harmful.
If serious mistakes go unmentioned, people may never realise that anything is wrong.
Imagine a manager who says nothing while an employee repeatedly mishandles money or treats customers badly.
Silence in such cases is not kindness, because it allows small problems to grow into serious ones.
A parent who ignores a child's dishonesty, by contrast, may quietly teach that lying carries no cost.
Some behavior is simply too important to be left uncorrected.
Gentle, honest correction is therefore just as necessary as praise.
In conclusion, praise is one of the most effective tools a teacher, parent, or employer can use.
But ignoring negative actions would leave people without the guidance they need to improve.
The best approach is to praise generously while still correcting mistakes with care.
